title: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)

references.label: Standard clinical hematology laboratory textbooks/manuals (e.g. Henry's Clinical Diagnosis and Management)

explanation: MCV expresses the average volume of a single red blood cell, calculated from the hematocrit and RBC count (on automated analyzers it is often measured directly by light-scatter/impedance sizing rather than calculated, but the relationship holds either way). MCV is the primary value used to classify anemia as microcytic, normocytic, or macrocytic — a classification, together with MCHC and clinical findings, that narrows the differential diagnosis rather than naming a specific cause.

workedExample.scenario: A hematocrit of 45% and an RBC count of 5.0 million/µL.

commonMistakes: Using hematocrit as a fraction (0.45) instead of a percentage (45) without adjusting the constant accordingly — the ×10 constant in this form assumes Hct is entered as a percentage.
